name: Rutherford
blurb: Mid-valley bench and alluvial fans famed for Cabernet (“Rutherford dust” lore); home to historic estates along Hwy 29 / Silverado Trail.

name: Oakville
blurb: Prime Cabernet territory between Yountville and Rutherford; To Kalon and other iconic vineyards. Climate point near Oakville crossroads.

name: Stags Leap District
blurb: East-side rocky soils and afternoon shade from the Stags Leap palisades; Cabernet that won the 1976 Judgment of Paris (Stag’s Leap Wine Cellars).

name: Calistoga
blurb: Warm northern end of the valley; volcanic soils, Cabernet and Zinfandel, plus historic Chateau Montelena nearby.

name: Los Carneros (shared)
blurb: Cool, windy AVA spanning southern Napa and Sonoma; Pinot Noir and Chardonnay (still and sparkling). Note: shared with Sonoma County.

name: Yountville
blurb: Southern valley floor AVA; Cabernet and Merlot with slightly cooler influence than Oakville/Rutherford.

name: Howell Mountain
blurb: Above the fog line on the eastern range; intense Cabernet and Merlot from volcanic soils at elevation.

name: St. Helena
blurb: Historic town and AVA in the north-central valley; Cabernet-focused with many classic estates along Hwy 29.

name: Mount Veeder
blurb: Mayacamas western mountains; steep vineyards, cooler nights, structured Cabernet and Chardonnay.

name: Atlas Peak
blurb: Eastern Vaca Range AVA; rocky volcanic soils and elevation for Cabernet and other Bordeaux varieties.

name: Coombsville
blurb: Eastern hills near the city of Napa; relatively cool pocket for Cabernet and Bordeaux blends.
